summary: Deschutes NF lookout on Cache Mountain built 1933 as a 20-ft pole tower; destroyed or removed in 1967 (sources differ on fire and year); footings photographed later, no current description found.

facts.design: 20-foot round pole tower with a 14x14 L-4 hip-roof cab, plus a 12x20 wood-frame garage
facts.status_note: Destroyed or removed in 1967, depending on the source; foundation blocks photographed in 2002 and footings shown in undated photos; no current description of the site found

staffing.status: lookouts placed on duty from 1931; last staffing in the sources read is a 1957 fire report, no later record

access.note: On Deschutes National Forest land reached by gravel forest roads, per Will Hite's account; no closure or permit rule found in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Will Hite drove FR 2066, FR 2068 and FR 800 from the Suttle Lake road; his page lists a hiking distance of 0 to 2.5 miles and says the roads are bad at the end. No official route described.

events.note: Deschutes NF placed two extra lookouts on duty in 1931; Wilbur Costello is named as one of them on Cache Mountain
A road was built to the summit the following year, and a phone line was run up from the Suttle Lake junction
Lyle Anderson spotted a smoke from the station on July 16, 1932 (Bend Bulletin item quoted on Forest Lookouts page)
20-foot round pole tower with L-4 cab, cost $910.84, plus a 12x20 wood-frame garage
Phillip Gould placed on Cache Mountain on July 16, 1937 (Bend Bulletin item quoted on Forest Lookouts page)
Station reported one fire during the 1957 season
Former Fire Lookout Sites register says the lookout nearly burned in the Big Lake Fire of 1966
Early September 1967 fire; an Oregonian report dated September 2, 1967 (quoted by Forest Lookouts) says it destroyed the Cash Mountain lookout post; Will Hite and firelookout.com also say destroyed
Former Fire Lookout Sites register says it was removed in 1967
Register photo captioned Foundation blocks, dated June 3, 2002
Registered January 4, 2011; nominated by Irene Potter

corrections.why: The register and the Forest Lookouts page both describe a 20-foot pole tower, about 6.1 m. 152.4 m is 500 feet, which no source read supports.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower nearly burned in the 1966 Big Lake Fire and was removed in 1967. Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1967. Will Hite and the Oregonian report quoted by Forest Lookouts describe a September 1967 fire that destroyed the lookout. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one cause.
The Oregonian text and Will Hite both print Cash Mountain. The Forest Service and the register use Cache Mountain, so the story uses Cache and treats Cash as a probable typo.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 152.4 is a data error; the tower was 20 ft. The 1966 vs 1967 and burned vs removed accounts conflict. No current description of the site or any closure was found; Will Hite's footings photos are undated. A Forest Service Facebook post on the 1967 fire could not be read (login wall), so it is not cited. The Cache Mountain RNA page covers the 2002 lightning fire, which is not a lookout fire but is included as the mountain's later fire history. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the Oregonian report is dated September 2, 1967; the Airstrip fire claim was removed because the report does not tie that fire to the lookout; 'Forest Lookouts register' corrected to 'Former Fire Lookout Sites register' (firetower.org); 'name different fires' overstatement removed.
